findings.title: Use the account UI's interpolation syntax instead of MessageFormat syntax
findings.body: This bundle is consumed by the account UI, whose existing messages use i18next-style placeholders such as `{{0}}` (and React component placeholders such as `<0>`). The new `{0}` and `{2,choice,...}` syntax is Java `MessageFormat` syntax and will not be evaluated by that UI, so validation errors will display literal `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}`, and the choice expression to account-console users. Keep the UI-compatible placeholder syntax and handle pluralization through the frontend's supported translation mechanism.

findings.title: Use the admin UI's interpolation syntax instead of MessageFormat syntax
findings.body: This resource is served to the JavaScript admin UI, where the surrounding validation messages use `{{0}}`-style interpolation. Replacing it with Java `MessageFormat` placeholders and a `choice` expression means the admin UI will render the expression literally rather than substituting the attribute and size values. This breaks the multivalued attribute validation message in the admin console.

findings.title: Lithuanian account message was replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The Lithuanian `totpStep1` translation is now `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian. Lithuanian account-console users will see an unrelated-language instruction while configuring an authenticator; restore a Lithuanian translation.

findings.title: Lithuanian login message was replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The Lithuanian `loginTotpStep1` translation is now `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian. This is displayed during the login OTP setup flow, so Lithuanian users receive the setup instruction in the wrong language; replace it with Lithuanian text.
